tEn: Designing for Agents: Zeno Rocha on Building Resend
tZh: 为智能体而设计：Zeno Rocha 谈打造 Resend
sEn: Resend founder Zeno Rocha shares how a developer-first email platform reached 4.3 million users and 10 million ARR.
sZh: Resend 创始人 Zeno Rocha 讲述开发者优先的邮件平台如何做到 430 万用户和 1000 万美元 ARR。

consensus.en: Resend now powers 4.3 million users and 120,000 paid customers, crossing SendGrid SDK downloads.
consensus.zh: Resend 现已服务 430 万用户、12 万付费客户，SDK 下载量已超过 SendGrid。

consensus.en: Email deliverability is an art and science: queue batching, IP pools, and engagement-based throttling.
consensus.zh: 邮件送达率是艺术与科学的结合：队列分批、IP 池和基于互动的限流。

consensus.en: Trust users by default, then detect and block abuse quickly via bounce and complaint signals.
consensus.zh: 默认信任用户，再通过退信和投诉信号快速识别并封禁滥用。

consensus.en: Bake best practices into the product—auto plain-text versions, insights, link and spell checkers.
consensus.zh: 把最佳实践内建进产品——自动纯文本版本、洞察、链接与拼写检查。

consensus.en: Being API-first and formless lets the product serve every surface: SDKs, CLI, MCP, agents.
consensus.zh: API 优先、无固定形态，让产品覆盖所有界面：SDK、CLI、MCP、智能体。

consensus.en: Domain reputation now matters more than IP; subdomains segregate transactional and marketing streams.
consensus.zh: 域名声誉如今比 IP 更重要；子域名可隔离事务性与营销邮件流。

contrarian.en: Removing signup friction and trusting users by default beats the industry's pre-approval gatekeeping.
contrarian.zh: 去掉注册摩擦、默认信任用户，胜过行业惯用的预审门槛。

contrarian.en: Owning the full stack down to the metal beats building on AWS SES despite the upfront cost.
contrarian.zh: 尽管前期成本高，自建底层基础设施仍胜过搭建在 AWS SES 之上。

contrarian.en: Rewriting tracking links to your own domain is bad; noisy-neighbor blacklisting can sink customers.
contrarian.zh: 把追踪链接改写到自己域名是坏事；邻居污染被拉黑会拖垮客户。

contrarian.en: More MCP tools, not fewer, is the right bet—80+ tools now, contrary to Cloudflare's two.
contrarian.zh: MCP 工具越多越好而非越少——现已 80 多个，与 Cloudflare 的两个相反。

contrarian.en: Every SDK is humanly generated, even for 400 users, because language experience matters.
contrarian.zh: 每个 SDK 都人工编写，哪怕只有 400 用户，因为语言体验很重要。

contrarian.en: He'd rather have a $10M ARR company and a close daughter than $100M and distance.
contrarian.zh: 他宁愿要 1000 万美元 ARR 的公司和亲密的女儿，也不要 1 亿与疏远。

turns.en: Yeah, there's just a lot of different things you can do because landing on the inbox, especially when you're doing high volume is different from like when you're scaling just like an app where you throw GPU at the problem or you just scale more vertically or horizontally, whatever it is. With email you got to respect the rules of the game and how Gmail behaves is differently from Outlook and differently from Yahoo Mail and it's an industry that is fascinating because it's so old school and it relies a lot on contacts. But what we found early on was like okay, we know nothing about this world and so coming from this perspective like extremely naive was the best thing that ever happened. Uh like honestly like it was the best thing because like there's no preconception of what is right, what is wrong. So for them, for example, every single app you go and then first thing you see is like this form that you got to fill out about like how many emails we're going to send, what's the volume, what are you trying to do? And then you go through a human verification process. Two days later, they accept you or deny you. Most of the times they're going to deny you. And I was like, this doesn't make any sense, right? Like why are we blocking people? So I know I'm going to remove that friction completely and the friction will be on us. We're going to figure that out. Of course, now four years, three years in into this business, I get it why they do that. There's just so much fraud and phishing and abuse across the board. I don't talk too much publicly about that, but we build like all sorts of crazy systems internally for that. But to your question, like how you architect that? Like for example, when you're sending an email to 100,000 people, if you just throw 100,000 emails like to Gmail, what Gmail will do is they're going to throttle the emails because it's way too much and they want to see the engagement. So what do you do is like they see like, okay, are people opening the emails? Are people archiving, deleting right away or not interacting? Okay, depending on those initial interactions, then what I'm going to do with the rest of the emails will dictate that beginning. So there clever things you can do where 100,000 people put the most engaged audience members in the beginning of that queue. You have to put that in a queue. You need to it's an art and a science where you got to space out each batch. So and space out between the different providers too. And yeah, now we're like buying different IP blocks. You got to look at the history of the IP blocks, distributed folks into different IP pools, and then balance the IP pools over time. So it's a whole crazy infrastructure game.
turns.zh: 是的，你可以做很多不同的事情，因为进入收件箱，尤其是当你进行大量发送时，与扩展一个应用不同，后者可以通过投入 GPU 或垂直/水平扩展来解决。对于电子邮件，你必须遵守游戏规则，Gmail 的行为与 Outlook 不同，与 Yahoo Mail 也不同，这个行业很有趣，因为它非常老派，并且很大程度上依赖联系人。但我们早期发现，我们对这个领域一无所知，所以从这种极其天真的视角出发是发生过的最好的事情。老实说，这是最好的事情，因为没有先入为主的观念什么是对什么是错。例如，对于他们来说，每个应用你进去首先看到的是一个表格，你必须填写关于我们要发送多少电子邮件、数量、你想做什么。然后你经过人工验证过程。两天后，他们接受或拒绝你。大多数时候他们会拒绝你。我当时想，这说不通，对吧？为什么要阻止人们？所以我知道我要完全消除这种摩擦，摩擦将由我们承担。我们会解决这个问题。当然，现在进入这个业务三四年了，我明白他们为什么这样做。到处都是欺诈和网络钓鱼和滥用。我不太公开谈论这个，但我们在内部构建了各种疯狂的系统来应对。但回答你的问题，如何架构这个？例如，当你向 10 万人发送电子邮件时，如果你只是向 Gmail 扔 10 万封电子邮件，Gmail 会限制电子邮件，因为太多了，他们想看到参与度。所以你要做的是，他们看到，好的，人们在打开电子邮件吗？人们在归档、立即删除还是不互动？好的，根据这些初始互动，然后我将如何处理其余的电子邮件将决定那个开始。所以你可以做聪明的事情，将 10 万人中最活跃的受众成员放在队列的开头。你必须把它放在队列中。你需要这是一种艺术和科学，你必须间隔每批发送。所以也要在不同提供商之间间隔。是的，现在我们购买不同的 IP 块。你必须查看 IP 块的历史，将人们分配到不同的 IP 池，然后随着时间的推移平衡 IP 池。所以这是一个疯狂的基础设施游戏。
